system_description: ZKasper: a RISC Zero zkVM guest that proves Ethereum Casper FFG finality. The host prepares SSZ Merkle multiproofs of beacon state fields plus uncompressed BLS public keys plus state patches; the guest verifies those proofs inside the zkVM, reconstructs validator committees via RANDAO-based shuffle, verifies BLS aggregate signatures over attestations, applies Casper FFG state-transition rules, and commits (pre_state, post_state) as the public journal.

attacker_controlled_inputs: input_bytes (Input<E>): attestations array, consensus_state checkpoint fields — deserialized from env::read_frame() with bincode inside the guest
ssz_reader_bytes (StateInput): beacon_block multiproof, beacon_state multiproof, active_validators multiproof, public_keys Vec, patches BTreeMap — all supplied by the (untrusted) host
StatePatch.randao_mixes (host-supplied, unverified RANDAO values for future epochs)
trust_roots: consensus_state.finalized_checkpoint.root — the only externally-anchored root; everything chains from it
RISC Zero journal commitment: only pre_state and post_state ABI-encoded bytes are public outputs
unverified_data: StatePatch.randao_mixes: accepted from host with only plausibility checks in validate_state_patches (churn limit, future-epoch assertions); no Merkle proof of RANDAO values
StatePatch.validator_exits: validated for churn-limit plausibility but 'once only' and ordering checks use assert!() not Result<>
public_keys Vec: matched against compressed chunks in proof but PublicKey::deserialize can panic on invalid input

critical_paths.name: BLS aggregate signature verification
critical_paths.risk: Depends on correct domain binding (genesis_validators_root, fork, epoch). Domain comes from StateReader::genesis_validators_root() and StateReader::fork() — both served from SSZ proof, verified chain.
critical_paths.notes: eth_fast_aggregate_verify semantics: empty pubkey list returns false (guarded by empty-attestation check). Slashed validators are excluded from balance but still included in pubkey list for signature verification — must confirm this is intentional.

critical_paths.name: Casper FFG state transition
critical_paths.key_concern: Only 1-finality and 2-finality paths trigger finalization. The verify() loop asserts exactly one finalization occurs. Code path: link source must equal current_justified or previous_justified checkpoint — checked by value equality, not by epoch range alone.
critical_paths.risk: LOW — well-tested with explicit test vectors including mainnet inactivity-leak cases.

critical_paths.name: SSZ multiproof Merkle verification
critical_paths.key_concern: descriptor-driven stack algorithm; CHUNK_SIZE is a const generic defaulting to 32; no explicit check that data.len() == node_count * CHUNK_SIZE before index arithmetic; panic path via assert_eq!(stack.len(), 1) and panic('root must be computed').
critical_paths.risk: Panics in guest = proof abort. Malformed multiproof can cause OOB slice in &data[node_index * CHUNK_SIZE..(node_index+1)*CHUNK_SIZE] if node_index overflows relative to data length.

critical_paths.name: RANDAO seed derivation (committee shuffle)
critical_paths.key_concern: Seed = SHA-256(domain_type_bytes || epoch_le_bytes || randao_mix). The randao_mix is fetched from StatePatch.randao_mixes — host-supplied and NOT Merkle-proven. An adversarial host can supply wrong RANDAO, causing the shuffle to produce a different committee assignment, which could cause signature verification to pass or fail arbitrarily.
critical_paths.risk: HIGH — unproven RANDAO is the most significant trust assumption in the system.

critical_paths.name: Validator multiproof extraction and public-key matching
critical_paths.key_concern: compressed-chunk matching via has_compressed_chunks(); uncompressed public keys are supplied out-of-band in public_keys Vec; PublicKey::deserialize() is called without error handling in to_validator_info() (conversions.rs:73). Panics on invalid input.
critical_paths.risk: MEDIUM — host controls public_keys; a mismatched or invalid key causes panic inside the guest.

critical_paths.name: State patch validation (validator exits)
critical_paths.key_concern: Uses assert!() macros (not Result) to enforce 'exit_epoch must change only once', ordering, and churn-limit constraints. assert!() panics abort the RISC Zero proof, but do NOT produce a meaningful error. Churn calculation uses a 2x multiplier described as 'seems reasonable' with a shrug emoji, suggesting it is not formally derived.
critical_paths.risk: MEDIUM — adversarial host can craft a patch that is slightly outside the valid window, triggering abort; or craft a patch slightly inside to inject a validator exit that inflates or deflates quorum.

dimension_map_anomalies.protocol_context: Affects entire committee assignment for all epochs covered by patch
dimension_map_anomalies.finding: UNKNOWN dimension — no proof binding this value to on-chain state

dimension_map_anomalies.trust_level: UNTRUSTED — host-supplied, matched only against compressed multiproof chunks
dimension_map_anomalies.semantic_role: BLS public keys for signature verification
dimension_map_anomalies.finding: Matching is done byte-for-byte against compressed chunks; deserialize() called without error recovery

dimension_map_anomalies.semantic_role: Exit epoch overrides that affect active validator set
dimension_map_anomalies.finding: No Merkle proof; host can understate exits (inflating validator count) or overstate (deflating) within churn tolerance

threat_model_notes: Replay: consensus_state.finalized_checkpoint is the chain-anchoring root; BLS signing domain includes genesis_validators_root and fork version — provides replay resistance across chains and forks.
RANDAO manipulation: RANDAO is unproven; host supplies future-epoch RANDAO without on-chain proof. This is the single largest trust gap.
Downgrade: Config.min_version / max_version restrict fork to Electra only; fork is checked against ChainSpec in ssz_state_reader — downgrade resistance present.
CSPRNG: No keygen or nonce generation in guest code; all randomness comes from RANDAO — appropriate for consensus protocol.
Sanitized checkpoints: trusted_checkpoint comes from pre-existing ConsensusState committed in the journal; attacker cannot forge it without breaking the zkVM proof binding.

open_findings.title: Unproven RANDAO in StatePatch enables adversarial committee manipulation
open_findings.description: StatePatch.randao_mixes values are host-supplied and accepted without any Merkle proof binding them to the on-chain beacon state. The seed derivation at get_seed() uses these values to compute the shuffling seed. An adversarial or compromised host can supply arbitrary RANDAO values to shift committee assignments, potentially causing a subset of validators to be assigned to a committee they would not otherwise control, undermining the BLS signature threshold check.

open_findings.title: Multiproof data bounds not validated before slice indexing
open_findings.description: The function indexes data as &data[node_index * CHUNK_SIZE..(node_index+1)*CHUNK_SIZE] but does not pre-validate that data.len() == (number of nodes from descriptor) * CHUNK_SIZE. A malformed or truncated multiproof from the host can cause a Rust slice panic (OOB) inside the guest, aborting proof generation. While this is a liveness/DoS issue rather than a soundness issue, it means the guest has no graceful error path for malformed host input.

open_findings.title: PublicKey::deserialize() panic on invalid host-supplied key
open_findings.description: PublicKey::deserialize(&v.public_key).unwrap() is called without error handling in to_validator_info(). In the guest context (called from into_state_reader()), an invalid or adversarially malformed public key in the public_keys Vec causes an unwrap panic inside the zkVM guest, aborting the proof. No liveness guarantee.

open_findings.title: validate_state_patches uses assert!() with a 2x churn-limit heuristic
open_findings.description: The churn budget is calculated as get_balance_churn_limit() * 2, with an inline comment 'seems reasonable ¯\_(ツ)_/¯', indicating the multiplier is not formally derived. If the true churn window allows fewer exits, an adversarial host can inject validator exits that pass this check but would be invalid on-chain, causing the active validator set to be incorrectly reduced. This deflates the quorum denominator, making the 2/3 supermajority threshold easier to meet.

open_findings.title: Commented-out head-state sanity check in find_finalization_epoch
open_findings.description: A sanity check that verifies the head state recognizes the trusted checkpoint as finalized is commented out. Without this check, the host may build an input that is accepted by an outdated or forked chain view, potentially feeding a stale or non-canonical state to the guest.
open_findings.severity_estimate: LOW — host-side only, does not affect zkVM soundness

open_findings.title: Slashed validators included in signature verification but excluded from balance
open_findings.description: get_attesting_indices() returns all attesting indices; these are mapped to pubkeys for BLS verification regardless of slashed status. The slashed filter is only applied when computing target_balance. This means a slashed validator's signature contributes to the aggregate signature check but not to the quorum threshold. Per the Ethereum spec this is intentional (slashed validators can still attest and their votes count for the aggregate but their balance is zeroed out for quorum), but it is worth confirming the spec alignment explicitly.
open_findings.severity_estimate: INFO — likely spec-correct, needs spec confirmation
